kaps_punt: Leesvaardighede: lees met begrip en vlotheid: Lees oor vaardighede om die vrede te bewaar en om as tussenganger op te tree: interpreteer/verduidelik en vertel wat aangeleer is.

items.bewering: „Julle is albei my maats. Ek kan help dat julle mekaar hoor as julle albei dit wil hê.” Sipho het sy skouers opgetrek en Ruan het stadig geknik. Toe het Sipho ook geknik.
items.bron: SkillsYouNeed, 'Peer Mediation' (skillsyouneed.com/ips/peer-mediation.html): mediation begins with consent ('I'm very happy to help with that'); Schrumpf et al. peer mediation model, UNCG (uncg.edu/~bblevin/class_management/models/pm.html): step 1 is 'agree to mediate'. The story shows the tussenganger offering help and both boys agreeing before she starts, which is the practice as described.
UNCG peer mediation model (Schrumpf, Crawford, Bodine): ground rule 'Mediator remains neutral'; SkillsYouNeed: peer mediators 'do not ... take sides'.

items.bewering: „Elkeen kry 'n beurt en die ander een luister tot hy klaar is. Niemand noem die ander een name nie.”
items.bron: UNCG peer mediation model: ground rules 'No name calling, insults ...' and 'No interrupting'; SkillsYouNeed: 'we will take it in turns to speak, and not interrupt each other.'

items.bewering: Lerato het ... gewag tot hy heeltemal klaar was. Toe het sy gesê wat sy gehoor het. „Jy het hard gewerk en nou is jy bekommerd oor Vrydag. Sê vir my as ek dit verkeerd het.” (en later dieselfde vir Ruan: „Jy het 'n moeilike week by die huis gehad ...”)
items.bron: SkillsYouNeed: 'After each person has set out their position, summarise what they have said to check that you, and the other person, have understood correctly'; UNCG model: 'the mediator summarizes what they have said.' The story's reflect-and-check matches, including restating feeling as well as content.

items.bewering: Lerato stop die gesprek wanneer Sipho 'n reël breek: „Dit was sy beurt en ons het gesê niemand noem die ander een name nie.”
items.bron: UNCG peer mediation model roleplay: the mediator holds the parties to settling it 'without name calling, and without interrupting each other'; the rules are agreed at the start and enforced by the mediator. The story's turn is consistent with the rules it set up earlier.

items.bewering: „Nou is dit julle twee se besluit. Ek gaan nie vir julle kies wat om te doen nie.” Die twee seuns stel self die oplossing voor (drie prente in plaas van ses, hulp met inkleur, oefen Donderdagmiddag).
items.bron: SkillsYouNeed: 'the problem or situation must remain "owned" by the participants, as must the solution or agreement'; UNCG model: 'Students create and own the solution.'

items.bewering: „Jy het 'n moeilike week by die huis gehad en die prente het deur die mat geval.”
items.bron: Maroela Media, 'Uitdrukking: Deur die mat val' (maroelamedia.co.za/afrikaans/idiome-en-uitdrukkings/uitdrukking-deur-die-mat-val/): the idiom means 'om te misluk' and is used of things and plans that do not come off, not only of people. Used here of the drawings that did not get done, the meaning fits. (Whether it is the best idiom for Grade 6 is a language question for the outside Afrikaans check, not a fact finding.)

items.bewering: Sipho het voorgestel dat Ruan net drie prente teken in plaas van ses ... By die derde prent het die hele klas begin lag.
items.bron: Internal consistency of the reading piece, checked against its own text: six drawings planned, three agreed, the third is shown; the timeline (work split two weeks earlier, argument Wednesday break, drawing that evening, colouring Thursday break, practice Thursday afternoon, talk Friday morning) holds without contradiction. The story's events are fiction and make no claim about the world beyond the mediation practice checked above.

opsomming: The reading piece is fiction whose only real-world claims are the peer-mediation steps it shows (consent first, no taking sides, turns and no name-calling, restating what each person said, the two parties choosing their own solution), and every one matches published peer-mediation guidance; there are no superlatives, dates or analogies, and nothing needs correcting.
